biography.plain_text: Paul Coulombe is a Maine entrepreneur who turned his father’s regional White Rock Distilleries into a national spirits business. After years building sales, he borrowed heavily to buy out his family, developed Three Olives and Pinnacle vodka, and sold the leading brands. He now owns and operates hospitality businesses in the Boothbay region.

long_biography.plain_text:
Travelling from bar to bar as a commission salesman taught Paul Coulombe how spirits brands reached customers. He joined White Rock Distilleries after university and spent two decades expanding its sales territory before taking control. His decisive bet was to build premium-looking vodka at accessible prices, pairing distinctive packaging with a widening flavour range.

After selling the spirits assets, Coulombe redirected his operating attention to coastal Maine. He rebuilt Boothbay Harbor Country Club and assembled nearby lodging and cottage businesses, treating tourism development as another hands-on enterprise. Maine recognised that work with the Governor’s Award for Tourism Excellence, while his current investment focus remains the country club and Boothbay Harbor Summer Cottages.
